label: Fires at GO after an unrewarded rare a2->S1 trial, growing later in the episode.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S1 u') * (ep_dec + 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * belief_lo
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (belief_lo < -2) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * (tv("action", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * belief_cover
explanation: Active only at GO. Magnitude is driven by the previous trial being a2 -> S1 (rare) unrewarded, the model-based stay-on-a2 case (GO residual +0.79 vs about -0.09 for all other histories). Within that case the activation grows strongly with episode time (ep_dec term), beyond the shared GO timing baseline. On the window first trial (previous trial unknown) it rises when the ideal observer believes S2 is good (negative belief_lo), standing in for the unseen a2-favouring history. Weaker belief dependence within the a2 S1 u case, the trial before, and belief_cover add almost nothing (free fit 0.594 vs short 0.591 dev). Residual misses are first-trial windows with large activation that belief only partly predicts. No future variables used.

issues: The label leaves out the third short-form term, which applies on the window's first trial and uses belief. A reader of the label alone could not predict the large first-trial activations, which make up most of the worst-fit windows (e.g. actual 2.9 vs predicted 0.23, 3.17 vs 0.19, 3.16 vs 0.21).

Core claim confirmed. The GO residual is +0.787 after a2 S1 u and about -0.086 after most other histories. last_is('a2 S1 u') alone scores test 0.502 beyond timing, and adding the ep_dec term gives 0.582-0.609. 'Every other history ~ -0.09' is loose: after a1 S1 u it is -0.038 and on the first trial ('?') it is -0.005.

The first-trial term is mis-specified. On the first trial, an unrewarded previous outcome (prev_reward == 0, which is observed) predicts better than belief alone: with the two a2 S1 u terms, (prev_action == -1)*(prev_reward == 0) gives test 0.604, (prev_action == -1)*belief_lo gives 0.593, and belief_lo < -2 gives 0.590.

Belief matters on more than the first trial. A GO*(prev_reward == 0)*belief_lo term covering every unrewarded trial, combined with last_is('a2 S1 u')*(ep_dec+1) and the first-trial unrewarded indicator, reaches test 0.627 (dev 0.626), against 0.593 for the recorded form. The explanation's claim that belief only stands in for history on the first trial is therefore incomplete.

Remaining systematic error: late-episode a2 S1 u GO steps after runs of a2 choices are under-predicted (actual 3-4 vs predicted ~1.25). Some activations after a2 S1 r are missed too (1.5 vs 0.11). Any of these short forms still under-predicts first-trial windows. None of this is a whole phase x previous-trial class beyond about 0.07 mean error, so the core reading holds.
